title: Casts from and to strings
verdict: strict parsing; shortest round-trip for doubles; no string → bool or date
description: Text to an integer accepts an optional sign and digits only (` 2`, `3.0`, `1e2`, `0x10` fail); text to a double accepts `nan`, `inf`, `-Infinity`, `.5`, `5.` and rounds `1e400` to inf. Failures raise with `strict=True` and are NULL with `strict=False`.

A double becomes its shortest round-trip text, with an exponent at 1e16 (`1e+16`) and at 1e-7 (`1e-7`), without one at 1e15 and 1e-5, `-0.0`, `inf` and `NaN`. Booleans become `true` and `false`; integers and doubles become booleans by `!= 0` (NaN is true).
Text to `Boolean` or to `Date` is refused (`InvalidOperationError`); `str.to_date` parses dates.
reference: Casts to and from strings follow the reference's `cast` rules; `cast_failure` as stated.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
